title: fix(plugin-form): never write the columns the server owns, and send only dirty cells in a master-detail batch
body:
Fixes #10108

Clause-②: no — measured from the diff, not asserted: the package publishes `.` only, built from `index.tsx`, and `index.tsx` does not re-export `sanitize`. After a build on this head, `grep -c SERVER_OWNED_FIELD_NAMES packages/plugin-form/dist/index.d.ts` prints `0`, and `filterSystemFields` / the rest of the face keep their signatures. Nothing an author writes changes; no accept set is relaxed; no public surface moves.

## Step 1 — what reproduced on today's `main`, and what did not

Everything on the card was relayed. It was re-derived here on `87af769e9` before a line was changed, with a probe that asserted the presence of the injected columns **and** the absence of ones the same filter already refused — so the finding is a live injection, not an absence a fixture invented.

**The payload-building sites.** Both paths the card names run through ONE builder, `sanitizeFormData` in `packages/plugin-form/src/sanitize.ts`:

- master-detail `POST /api/v1/batch` — `MasterDetailForm`'s `submitViaBatch` hands the parent values and each child collection to `buildMasterDetailEditBatch` / `buildMasterDetailBatch` in `packages/plugin-form/src/masterDetailTx.ts`; the child rows go through its `toWritable`, which calls `sanitizeFormData`. `LineItemsPanel`'s `save` is the second caller of the same builder.
- plain record edit `PATCH` — `ObjectForm`'s submit chain calls `sanitizeFormData(formData, objectSchema)` and hands the result to `saveWithOcc`.

**What reproduced, exactly as written.** One filter, two answers, in the same call on the same fixture:

| column | before this branch |
|:--|:--|
| `owner_id`, `owning_business_unit_id`, `created_by`, `updated_by` | **emitted** |
| `created_at`, `updated_at`, `organization_id`, `id` | refused (the control) |

That split is the whole diagnosis: the refusal is a hand-written NAME roster, and the emitted four were simply never in it. Nothing about the schema, the field types or the readonly flags distinguishes the two rows of that table — the injected columns are neither `hidden` nor `readonly`, because ownership is reassignable.

The card's two claims about the plain edit form both reproduced. A form declaring three business fields and no ownership column rendered two inputs and still sent `owner_id` — so the payload injects it rather than echoing a displayed field. And every child row was rewritten in full, including the two the user never touched.

**What did not reproduce as stated:** the card says the message naming the refused field "only appears in the network response". It also reaches the browser console — the renderer logs `[form] write denied:` with the whole error before it substitutes the user-facing text. See the secondary item below.

## What shipped — both tiers

**1. One roster, and the invariant it expresses.** The write-side roster in `sanitize.ts` and the render-side roster in `autoLayout.ts` were two hand-written copies of the same list. They drifted: the render copy had learned to drop `owner_id`, the write copy never did. They are now the same object, `SERVER_OWNED_FIELD_NAMES`, whose header carries the rationale — a form never writes a field it refuses to render. The unified list adds `owning_business_unit_id`, `company_id`, `space`, `_id`, `__v`, `created`, `modified`, `modified_by` and the camelCase ownership spellings to **both** sides.

⚠️ That is an observable narrowing on the render side too: an auto-laid-out form that was rendering one of those as an editable input no longer does. It is declared in the changeset.

**2. The flag, because a name list cannot shut the class.** `sanitizeFormData` now refuses any field the object schema marks `system: true` — the registry's own mark on everything it injects, the same flag `isSystemManagedField` in `@object-ui/types` reads. The next injected column needs no edit here. This is the half the triage comment asked for: the roster alone would let the next one bite the same way.

**3. Dirty fields only, in the batch.** A master-detail edit batch now sends only the cells that differ from the loaded snapshot, and a row where nothing moved emits **no operation at all** (every row with an id used to be routed to "update" whether or not anything had moved). The comparison resolves everything it cannot settle towards SENDING — `1000` and `'1000'` read as different, objects compare by serialization, and a snapshot that does not show a row already linked still gets its FK re-asserted. Saying "changed" about an equal pair costs one column on the wire; saying "unchanged" about a changed pair would discard a user's edit with a 200 back, and that is the one failure this diff must not have.

**4. The builder no longer trusts its caller.** `buildMasterDetailBatch` / `buildMasterDetailEditBatch` apply the roster to the PARENT payload too. Both production callers already hand it a sanitized payload, but that is the caller's habit, not the builder's contract — and a payload builder trusting what it was handed is this card's whole defect.

The measured end state for the card's own scenario — one cell changed on one of three child rows:

```
{"operations":[
  {"object":"kpi_entry_sheet","action":"update","id":"SHEET1","data":{"subject":"bu_sw_sales","status":"draft"}},
  {"object":"kpi_entry_line","action":"update","id":"a","data":{"actual_value":900}}],
 "atomic":true}
```

## Secondary item: NOT done, and why

The card asks for the server's message to reach the user. Left alone, per the dispatch's own instruction for when it needs more than a small local change — and it does, in the direction that matters: **doing it here would reverse a ruling, not fill a gap.**

The form renderer substitutes a localized `form.noPermissionToSave` for every permission denial on purpose. Its comment records why: rendering the server text verbatim put raw diagnostics in front of end users, untranslated and leaking the object's machine name and the record id, and that was ruled and repaired — the record is objectstack#3821, restated for a 403 at objectui#5210. Printing the refusal text again would reintroduce that for every permission denial in the product, not only this one.

⭐ And the seam for doing it correctly already exists, on the other side of the wire: `declaredUserMessage` reads `userMessage`, the producer-side marking a hook sets at throw time to say "this text is for the end user" (objectstack#9934). ⇒ The correct change is for the platform's ownership-transfer refusal to carry `userMessage`, after which this console surfaces it with no code change here at all. That is an objectstack change, outside this card's repo. Reported to the PM rather than filed.

Meanwhile the diagnosis is not invisible: the renderer logs the full error under `[form] write denied:` before substituting.

## Scope boundary I did not cross

The parent operation of a master-detail batch, and the plain record edit `PATCH`, still send the full sanitized form values rather than a dirty diff. The card scopes "send only dirty fields" to the batch, and the batch's child rows are where the snapshot lives: the parent's persisted record is fetched inside `ObjectForm` and never handed back out, so a parent dirty diff needs a new seam through the form's `submitHandler` contract — a wider change than this card, on the most-used write path in the product, where a false-clean silently drops a user's edit. The 403 no longer happens either way: it was caused by the roster, not by volume.

## Verification

Reverse verification, with the fix committed first so the restore leg has a real restore point. The three implementation files were reverted to the branch point, each mutation proven on disk by comparing `git hash-object` against the `HEAD` blob (three distinct hashes, no empty reads), restored under a `trap`, and the restore proven by `git diff HEAD` being empty:

```
MUTATED packages/plugin-form/src/sanitize.ts      HEAD=9bbbffaca432 -> disk=e6d07c267cfa
MUTATED packages/plugin-form/src/autoLayout.ts    HEAD=634f120185aa -> disk=9373fc11e754
MUTATED packages/plugin-form/src/masterDetailTx.ts HEAD=faa37e406e6c -> disk=d7ab7883d82a
grep -c owner_id packages/plugin-form/src/sanitize.ts  ->  0      (the defect itself: the roster never named it)
MUTATED RUN   Tests  11 failed | 11 passed (22)     exit 1
RESTORED      all three files match their HEAD blob, git diff HEAD empty
RESTORED RUN  Tests  22 passed (22)                 exit 0
```

All 11 reds are the new and retriaged pins, and they cover **both** paths — the `/batch` rows and the `plain record edit form PATCH` row both went red — plus two system-managed fields beyond `owner_id` (`owning_business_unit_id`, `created_by` / `updated_by`) and one that no roster in this repository names, refused by its `system` flag alone. No rebuild was needed for the ablation: all three files are consumed as sources through relative imports inside the same package, so nothing reads a `dist/`.

Checks on this head (`origin/main` merged in, so PR #10151's bundle-analysis repair for incident #10148 is included — that gate and its ceilings are untouched by this branch):

| check | command | result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| package tests | `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-form/` | **105 files, 1021 passed, 1 skipped**, exit 0 |
| typecheck | `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-form run type-check` (src + `tsconfig.test.json`) | exit 0 |
| lint | `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-form lint` | exit 0 — **136 files, 0 errors**, 899 warnings (the package's standing `no-explicit-any` baseline; the three in the new test file match its neighbours) |
| changeset presence | `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | exit 0 |
| changeset no-major / claims / pending-literals | `check:changeset-*`, `check:pending-changeset-literals` | exit 0 |
| line citations | `pnpm check:new-line-citations` | exit 0 — 0 new citations |
| control bytes | `pnpm check:control-bytes` | exit 0 |
| test path roots, unreferenced sources, metadata write doors, handler key reads | the matching `check:*` | exit 0 |

**Declared narrowing on the repo-wide lint.** `pnpm lint` is `turbo run lint`, i.e. each package's own `eslint .`; the run above IS that command for the one package this diff touches, over its whole tree rather than only the changed files. Every changed file lives in `packages/plugin-form` (plus one `.changeset/*.md`, which eslint does not read). `eslint.config.js` configures no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService`, so type-aware linting is not enabled and no rule in this repository can read across a file boundary — a change inside this package therefore cannot move the verdict on any file it does not touch. The remaining packages' lint runs are CI's.

Every exit code above was captured before any pipe. What is NOT measured here: remote CI, which has not run on this head yet.

## Acceptance notes

- The lifecycle bookkeeping columns (`locked`, `instance_state`, `deleted`, `is_deleted`) are deliberately left OUT of the roster. They are plausibly author-writable — a workflow form driving record state writes business meaning, not provenance — and nothing has measured them refusing a write. Adding one on the strength of the pattern alone would silently drop a value a form was asked to persist, which is the failure direction this module must not take.
- Three fixtures in `masterDetailTx.test.ts` were retriaged rather than deleted, because each pinned the pre-fix full-row rewrite. One of them, `emits only the parent update when children are unchanged`, was **false under its own name** before this branch: the batch also carried a full-row rewrite of the child. Its snapshot was also missing the back-reference FK the real loader always returns, so it has been given the runtime's shape, and a new row pins what the builder does with a snapshot that lacks it.
- The sanitize half of `update carries routing id but a sanitized data payload` was kept able to fail: the computed columns it asserts absent DIFFER from the snapshot, so only the sanitizer can be keeping them out — the dirty diff would let both through.
- Noted, not filed: `packages/types/src/system-fields.ts` holds a third roster of the same family (display-oriented) and `packages/plugin-detail` a fourth (inline-edit "never editable"). Each has a written reason to be separate and none is wrong today. Successor: none — nothing in flight touches them, and folding four purpose-specific rosters together is a decision, not a cleanup.
- Hands-off files named in the dispatch were not touched: `recordActivityFeed.ts` and the `record:history` row-cap path, `packages/plugin-calendar/**`, `useSettledSchema*`, and the three publish-drafts call sites in `app-shell`.
